title: Attention alerts, join-rules skips and capture failures are not persisted, so they cannot appear in the notification center
evidence: r1 attention alerts (packages/meeting-bot calendar/alerts), join-rules skips and capture failures are delivered by Telegram only; no tenant-scoped collection stores them (grep of packages/meeting-bot and apps/api/src/join-rules finds no event write). GET /notifications therefore covers only upload-queue, provider-job and watcher failures.
fix_direction: Owner decision: a notifications/events collection (schema, migration, write sites, retention, per-tenant read state), then a unit that writes and reads it.

title: Read/unread is client-side only (localStorage); no server store, no header bell or unread badge
evidence: No server collection exists for read state, so marks live in one browser and are not shared across devices. A shell-wide bell would poll /notifications on every page; not built, the page /notifications is the entry.
fix_direction: Depends on ISS-NOTIFCENTER-001 owner decision; bell/badge after a persisted store exists.

title: Windowed aggregation: failures older than each source newest-N rows are not seen; upload-queue source is single-tenant by configuration
evidence: Each source is read with the same limit (max 100) and filtered to failures afterwards, so a failure older than the newest N rows of its source is missed (truncated flag is set when a source has older rows). activity-health reads only the UPLOAD_TENANT_ID tenant, so other tenants see upload-queue as unavailable. Also apps/api/src/activity-health/router.test.ts end-to-end Python test fails on base (ISS-T057OPS-002).
fix_direction: Failure-filtered reads per source would need new store methods; deferred.

title: Read marks in localStorage are keyed by notification id only, not per tenant/key
evidence: notificationsClient.ts STORAGE_KEY lkbNotificationsRead is one global key; loadReadIds runs once at mount. Another tenant signing in on the same browser keeps the previous tenant's opaque ids (job/run ids, no content) and they share the 500-id cap, so marks can be evicted. Counts are computed from the current response only, so no previous-tenant count or content is shown.
fix_direction: Key by a hash of tenant (or clear on sign-out) once /whoami-style tenant id is available client-side; found by checker t057-notification-center.
